---
title: "Pre-Build Workflows"
description: "Configure how Revolte reviews, summarizes, and prepares generated changes before they reach human reviewers."
---

Pre-build workflows allow Revolte to perform automated review passes and summarization on generated changes. This ensures that every pull request is high-quality, well-documented, and follows your team's conventions before a human ever looks at it.

## Open YML Configuration

To configure these workflows, select your project, open the application, and navigate to **YML Configuration**. Use the **Repo Preference** tab to manage pre-build behavior.

<Steps>
  <Step title="Select the project">
    From the dashboard, go to **Projects** and open the project that contains the application.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Open the application">
    Choose the application repository you want Revolte to configure.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Open YML Configuration">
    Select **YML Configuration**, then use **Repo Preference** to configure repository and pre-build behavior.
  </Step>
</Steps>

## Code Review and Summarisation

The **Code Review and Summarisation** section defines how Revolte should comment on and document generated changes.

<CardGroup cols={2}>
  <Card title="Summarize Intent" icon="list">
    Revolte adds a concise summary of the generated change to the pull request description, explaining the *why* and *how* of the implementation.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Suggest Fixes" icon="wrench">
    If Revolte detects a potential issue during its own review pass, it can leave inline fix suggestions directly on the pull request.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Comment Style" icon="message-square">
    Choose between **balanced**, **concise**, or **verbose** review styles depending on the level of detail your team prefers.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Exclude Files" icon="file-x">
    Specify files or extensions (like lockfiles or generated assets) that should be ignored by the automated review pass.
  </Card>
</CardGroup>

## When to Use

Use pre-build workflows when:
- You want to ensure consistent pull request descriptions across the team.
- You have a complex codebase where an initial automated review pass helps catch edge cases.
- You want to reduce the "review fatigue" of human developers by catching simple issues early.

<Note title="Manual Review Still Applies">
  While Revolte performs an automated pass, these workflows are designed to *assist* your team. Human review remains the final authority before merging code into production.
</Note>
